sanskrit: sulabhaḥ suvrataḥ siddhaḥ śatrujic chatrutāpanaḥ nyagrodhodumbaro 'śvatthaś cāṇūrāndhraniṣūdanaḥ
english: He is easily attained, of noble vows, the Perfected One, vanquisher of foes, scorcher of foes; the banyan, the fig, the holy aśvattha tree, the slayer of Cāṇūra of the Andhras.

sanskrit: sahasrārciḥ saptajihvaḥ saptaidhāḥ saptavāhanaḥ amūrtir anagho 'cintyo bhayakṛd bhayanāśanaḥ
english: Of a thousand rays, seven-tongued, seven-fuelled, borne by seven steeds; formless, sinless, inconceivable, maker of fear and destroyer of fear.

sanskrit: aṇur bṛhat kṛśaḥ sthūlo guṇabhṛn nirguṇo mahān adhṛtaḥ svadhṛtaḥ svāsyaḥ prāgvaṃśo vaṃśavardhanaḥ
english: The atom and the vast, the slender and the gross, bearer of the qualities yet beyond all qualities, the great; unsupported yet self-supported, fair of face, ancient of lineage, increaser of lineage.

sanskrit: bhārabhṛt kathito yogī yogīśaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ kṣāmaḥ suparṇo vāyuvāhanaḥ
english: Bearer of the burden, the proclaimed one, the yogin, lord of yogins, granter of every desire; the resting-place, the toiler, the patient, the fair-winged, borne upon the wind.

sanskrit: dhanurdharo dhanurvedo daṇḍo damayitā damaḥ aparājitaḥ sarvasaho niyantā niyamo yamaḥ
english: Bearer of the bow, the science of archery, the rod of chastisement, the subduer, restraint itself; unconquered, all-enduring, the controller, discipline, the curber.

sanskrit: sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ abhiprāyaḥ priyārho 'rhaḥ priyakṛt prītivardhanaḥ
english: Endowed with goodness, of the nature of sattva, the True, devoted to truth and righteousness; the goal of intention, worthy of love, the worshipful, doer of what is dear, increaser of delight.

sanskrit: vihāyasagatir jyotiḥ surucir hutabhug vibhuḥ ravir virocanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravilocanaḥ
english: He whose path is the sky, the Light, of fair radiance, the eater of oblations, the all-pervading; the sun, the shining one, Sūrya, the impeller, whose eye is the sun.

sanskrit: ananto hutabhug bhoktā sukhado naikado 'grajaḥ anirviṇṇaḥ sadāmarṣī lokādhiṣṭhānam adbhutam
english: The endless, eater of oblations, the enjoyer, giver of bliss, the manifold giver, the first-born; never wearied, ever forbearing, the wondrous foundation of the worlds.

sanskrit: sanāt sanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapir avyayaḥ svastidaḥ svastikṛt svasti svastibhuk svastidakṣiṇaḥ
english: The eternal, most ancient of the ancient, Kapila, the tawny one, the imperishable; giver of weal, maker of weal, weal itself, enjoyer of weal, bestower of weal as his largesse.

sanskrit: araudraḥ kuṇḍalī cakrī vikramy ūrjitaśāsanaḥ śabdātigaḥ śabdasahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarīkaraḥ
english: Free of fury, wearer of earrings, bearer of the discus, the valiant, of mighty command; beyond the reach of words, enduring all sound, the cool one, maker of the night.

sanskrit: akrūraḥ peśalo dakṣo dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇāṃ varaḥ vidvattamo vītabhayaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ
english: The gentle, the graceful, the able, the dexterous, best among the forbearing; most learned, free of fear, the hearing and proclaiming of whom is holy.

sanskrit: uttāraṇo duṣkṛtihā puṇyo duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ vīrahā rakṣaṇaḥ santo jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ
english: The deliverer, destroyer of evil deeds, the holy, dispeller of evil dreams; slayer of heroes, the protector, the existent, the life, the all-abiding.

sanskrit: anantarūpo 'nantaśrīr jitamanyur bhayāpahaḥ caturasro gabhīrātmā vidiśo vyādiśo diśaḥ
english: Of endless forms, of endless splendour, conqueror of wrath, remover of fear; foursquare, of profound nature, the intermediate quarters, the commander, the directions themselves.

sanskrit: anādir bhūr bhuvo lakṣmīḥ suvīro rucirāṅgadaḥ janano janajanmādir bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: The beginningless, the earth, the splendour of the firmament, the valiant, wearer of gleaming armlets; the begetter, origin of the birth of creatures, the terrible, of terrible prowess.

sanskrit: ādhāranilayo dhātā puṣpahāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ ūrdhvagaḥ satpathācāraḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ
english: The abode of all support, the ordainer, whose laughter is the bursting of blossoms, the ever-wakeful; the upward-mover, treader of the path of the good, giver of breath, the sacred Oṃ, the pledge.

sanskrit: pramāṇaṃ prāṇanilayaḥ prāṇakṛt prāṇajīvanaḥ tattvaṃ tattvavid ekātmā janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ
english: The measure, the resting-place of life-breath, maker of breath, the life of the breath; the Reality, knower of Reality, the one Self, who transcends birth, death, and old age.

sanskrit: bhūr bhuvaḥ svas tarus tāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ yajño yajñapatir yajvā yajñāṅgo yajñavāhanaḥ
english: Earth, mid-air, and heaven, the tree, the deliverer, the impeller, the great-grandsire; the sacrifice, lord of the sacrifice, the sacrificer, the limb of sacrifice, the vehicle of sacrifice.

sanskrit: yajñabhṛd yajñakṛd yajñī yajñabhug yajñasādhanaḥ yajñāntakṛd yajñaguhyam annam annāda eva ca
english: Upholder of sacrifice, performer of sacrifice, the sacrificer, enjoyer of sacrifice, the means of sacrifice; bringer of sacrifice to its end, the mystery of sacrifice, the food, and the eater of food as well.

sanskrit: ātmayoniḥ svayaṃjāto vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ
english: Self-originated, self-born, the digger-forth, the singer of the Sāman chants; the joy of Devakī, the creator, lord of the earth, destroyer of sin.

sanskrit: śaṅkhabhṛn nandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ rathāṅgapāṇir akṣobhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ
english: Bearer of the conch, wielder of the Nandaka sword, holder of the discus, armed with the Śārṅga bow, bearer of the mace; whose hand holds the chariot-wheel, the unshakable, armed with every weapon of war.

sanskrit: itīdaṃ kīrtanīyasya keśavasya mahātmanaḥ nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ divyānām aśeṣeṇa prakīrtitam
english: Thus has this thousand of the divine names of the praiseworthy and great-souled Keśava been wholly proclaimed.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ yaś cāpi parikīrtayet nāśubhaṃ prāpnuyāt kiṃ cit so 'mutreha ca mānavaḥ
english: The man who listens to this daily, and who also recites it, shall meet with nothing inauspicious, neither here nor in the world beyond.

sanskrit: vedāntago brāhmaṇaḥ syāt kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet vaiśyo dhanasamṛddhaḥ syāc chūdraḥ sukham avāpnuyāt
english: A brāhmaṇa shall reach the end of the Veda, a kṣatriya shall become victorious, a vaiśya shall grow rich in wealth, and a śūdra shall attain happiness.

sanskrit: dharmārthī prāpnuyād dharmam arthārthī cārtham āpnuyāt kāmān avāpnuyāt kāmī prajārthī cāpnuyāt prajāḥ
english: He who seeks righteousness shall gain righteousness, he who seeks wealth shall obtain wealth, he who desires shall win his desires, and he who longs for offspring shall obtain offspring.

sanskrit: bhaktimān yaḥ sadotthāya śucis tadgatamānasaḥ sahasraṃ vāsudevasya nāmnām etat prakīrtayet
english: The devoted man who, ever rising at dawn, purified and with his mind fixed upon Him, recites this thousand of the names of Vāsudeva—

sanskrit: yaśaḥ prāpnoti vipulaṃ jñātiprādhānyam eva ca acalāṃ śriyam āpnoti śreyaś cāpnoty anuttamam
english: —attains abundant fame and preeminence among his kinsmen; he gains unshaken fortune and the highest, unsurpassed welfare.

sanskrit: na bhayaṃ kva cid āpnoti vīryaṃ tejaś ca vindati bhavaty arogo dyutimān balarūpaguṇānvitaḥ
english: He meets with fear nowhere, and gains valour and lustre; he becomes free of disease, radiant, endowed with strength, beauty, and virtue.

sanskrit: rogārto mucyate rogād baddho mucyeta bandhanāt bhayān mucyeta bhītaś ca mucyetāpanna āpadaḥ
english: One afflicted by disease is freed from disease, one bound is freed from bondage, the frightened is freed from fear, and one in distress is freed from his distress.

sanskrit: durgāṇy atitaraty āśu puruṣaḥ puruṣottamam stuvan nāmasahasreṇa nityaṃ bhaktisamanvitaḥ
english: A man swiftly crosses over all hardships who, with this thousand of names, praises the Supreme Person daily and full of devotion.

sanskrit: vāsudevāśrayo martyo vāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti brahma sanātanam
english: The mortal who takes refuge in Vāsudeva, who is wholly devoted to Vāsudeva, his soul cleansed of every sin, attains to the eternal Brahman.

sanskrit: na vāsudevabhaktānām aśubhaṃ vidyate kva cit janmamṛtyujarāvyādhibhayaṃ vāpy upajāyate
english: For the devotees of Vāsudeva there exists nothing inauspicious anywhere; nor does there arise in them any fear of birth, death, old age, or disease.

sanskrit: imaṃ stavam adhīyānaḥ śraddhābhaktisamanvitaḥ yujyetātmasukhakṣāntiśrīdhṛtismṛtikīrtibhiḥ
english: He who recites this hymn, endowed with faith and devotion, shall be joined with inner happiness, patience, fortune, steadfastness, memory, and renown.

sanskrit: na krodho na ca mātsaryaṃ na lobho nāśubhā matiḥ bhavanti kṛtapuṇyānāṃ bhaktānāṃ puruṣottame
english: Neither anger, nor envy, nor greed, nor any base intent arises in those of accumulated merit who are devoted to the Supreme Person.

sanskrit: dyauḥ sacandrārkanakṣatrā khaṃ diśo bhūr mahodadhiḥ vāsudevasya vīryeṇa vidhṛtāni mahātmanaḥ
english: The heaven with its moon, sun, and stars, the sky, the quarters, the earth, and the great ocean—all are upheld by the might of the great-souled Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: sasurāsuragandharvaṃ sayakṣoragarākṣasam jagad vaśe vartatedaṃ kṛṣṇasya sacarācaram
english: This whole world, with its gods, asuras, and gandharvas, with its yakṣas, serpents, and rākṣasas, with all that moves and moves not, abides under the sway of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi mano buddhiḥ sattvaṃ tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ vāsudevātmakāny āhuḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrajña eva ca
english: The senses, the mind, the intellect, goodness, lustre, strength, and steadfastness—these they declare to have Vāsudeva for their essence, as too the field and the knower of the field.

sanskrit: sarvāgamānām ācāraḥ prathamaṃ parikalpyate ācāraprabhavo dharmo dharmasya prabhur acyutaḥ
english: Right conduct is reckoned the foremost of all the scriptures; righteousness springs from conduct, and the lord of righteousness is Acyuta, the Imperishable.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā mahābhūtāni dhātavaḥ jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ cedaṃ jagan nārāyaṇodbhavam
english: The seers, the ancestors, the gods, the great elements, the bodily constituents, and this whole world of the moving and the unmoving—all spring from Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: yogo jñānaṃ tathā sāṃkhyaṃ vidyāḥ śilpāni karma ca vedāḥ śāstrāṇi vijñānam etat sarvaṃ janārdanāt
english: Yoga, knowledge, and Sāṃkhya, the sciences, the crafts, and ritual action, the Vedas, the treatises, and discernment—all this comes forth from Janārdana.

sanskrit: eko viṣṇur mahad bhūtaṃ pṛthag bhūtāny anekaśaḥ trīṃl lokān vyāpya bhūtātmā bhuṅkte viśvabhug avyayaḥ
english: Viṣṇu is the one great Being, yet the beings are manifold and severally apart; pervading the three worlds, the Soul of all beings, the imperishable enjoyer of the universe, He enjoys them all.

sanskrit: imaṃ stavaṃ bhagavato viṣṇor vyāsena kīrtitam paṭhed ya icchet puruṣaḥ śreyaḥ prāptuṃ sukhāni ca
english: This hymn of the Lord Viṣṇu, proclaimed by Vyāsa, let that man recite who wishes to attain welfare and happiness.

sanskrit: viśveśvaram ajaṃ devaṃ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam bhajanti ye puṣkarākṣaṃ na te yānti parābhavam
english: Those who worship the lotus-eyed Lord of the universe, the unborn god, the origin and dissolution of the world, never come to defeat.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ke pūjyāḥ ke namaskāryāḥ kathaṃ varteta keṣu ca kimācāraḥ kīdṛśeṣu pitāmaha na riṣyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who are to be honoured, who are to be saluted, how should one conduct oneself, and toward whom? What conduct, and toward what sort of men, O grandsire, brings no harm?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇānāṃ paribhavaḥ sādayed api devatāḥ brāhmaṇānāṃ namaskartā yudhiṣṭhira na riṣyate
english: Bhīṣma said: Contempt of the brāhmaṇas would lay low even the gods; he who salutes the brāhmaṇas, O Yudhiṣṭhira, comes to no harm.

sanskrit: te pūjyās te namaskāryā vartethās teṣu putravat te hi lokān imān sarvān dhārayanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: They are to be honoured, they are to be saluted; conduct yourself toward them as a son, for those wise ones uphold all these worlds.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ sarvalokānāṃ mahānto dharmasetavaḥ dhanatyāgābhirāmāś ca vāksaṃyamaratāś ca ye
english: The brāhmaṇas are the great ones of all the worlds, the bridges of righteousness, delighting in the renunciation of wealth and devoted to restraint of speech.

sanskrit: ramaṇīyāś ca bhūtānāṃ nidhānaṃ ca dhṛtavratāḥ praṇetāraś ca lokānāṃ śāstrāṇāṃ ca yaśasvinaḥ
english: Delightful to all beings and their treasure-house, firm in their vows, the guides of the worlds, and the renowned masters of the scriptures.

sanskrit: tapo yeṣāṃ dhanaṃ nityaṃ vāk caiva vipulaṃ balam prabhavaś cāpi dharmāṇāṃ dharmajñāḥ sūkṣmadarśinaḥ
english: Those whose wealth is ever their austerity and whose speech is their abundant strength, who are the source of all duties, knowers of righteousness, and seers of the subtle.

sanskrit: dharmakāmāḥ sthitā dharme sukṛtair dharmasetavaḥ yān upāśritya jīvanti prajāḥ sarvāś caturvidhāḥ
english: Lovers of righteousness, established in righteousness, bridges of righteousness by their good deeds, upon whom all creatures of the four kinds depend for their living.

sanskrit: panthānaḥ sarvanetāro yajñavāhāḥ sanātanāḥ pitṛpaitāmahīṃ gurvīm udvahanti dhuraṃ sadā
english: They are the paths, the leaders of all, the eternal bearers of sacrifice, who ever carry the heavy yoke handed down from fathers and forefathers.

sanskrit: dhuri ye nāvasīdanti viṣame sadgavā iva pitṛdevātithimukhā havyakavyāgrabhojinaḥ
english: Who, like good oxen, do not sink beneath the yoke on rough ground, who set the ancestors, the gods, and guests foremost, and eat only after the offerings to gods and ancestors.

sanskrit: bhojanād eva ye lokāṃs trāyante mahato bhayāt dīpāḥ sarvasya lokasya cakṣuś cakṣuṣmatām api
english: Who by that very eating save the worlds from great peril; they are the lamps of all the world, the very eye even of those who have eyes.

sanskrit: sarvaśilpādinidhayo nipuṇāḥ sūkṣmadarśinaḥ gatijñāḥ sarvabhūtānām adhyātmagaticintakāḥ
english: Treasuries of all crafts and lore, skilled, seers of the subtle, knowers of the courses of all beings, ponderers of the path of the inner Self.

sanskrit: ādimadhyāvasānānāṃ jñātāraś chinnasaṃśayāḥ parāvaraviśeṣajñā gantāraḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: Knowers of the beginning, the middle, and the end, their doubts cut away, discerners of the distinction between the high and the low, travellers to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: vimuktā dhutapāpmāno nirdvaṃdvā niṣparigrahāḥ mānārhā mānitā nityaṃ jñānavidbhir mahātmabhiḥ
english: Liberated, their sins shaken off, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of possessions, worthy of honour and ever honoured by the great-souled knowers of wisdom.

sanskrit: candane malapaṅke ca bhojane 'bhojane samāḥ samaṃ yeṣāṃ dukūlaṃ ca śāṇakṣaumājināni ca
english: The same toward sandal-paste and toward foul mire, the same in eating and in fasting; to whom fine silk and coarse hemp, linen, and skins are all alike.

sanskrit: tiṣṭheyur apy abhuñjānā bahūni divasāny api śoṣayeyuś ca gātrāṇi svādhyāyaiḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ
english: They can abide without eating even for many days, and with senses controlled they wear down their bodies by the study of the sacred texts.

sanskrit: adaivaṃ daivataṃ kuryur daivataṃ cāpy adaivatam lokān anyān sṛjeyuś ca lokapālāṃś ca kopitāḥ
english: They could make a god of what is no god and a no-god of a god; when angered they could create other worlds and other world-guardians.

sanskrit: apeyaḥ sāgaro yeṣām abhiśāpān mahātmanām yeṣāṃ kopāgnir adyāpi daṇḍake nopaśāmyati
english: By whose curse, great-souled as they are, the ocean became undrinkable, and whose fire of wrath even to this day is not quenched in the Daṇḍaka forest.

sanskrit: devānām api ye devāḥ kāraṇaṃ kāraṇasya ca pramāṇasya pramāṇaṃ ca kas tān abhibhaved budhaḥ
english: They who are gods even of the gods, the cause of the cause, and the authority of authority itself—what wise man could overpower them?

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ vṛddhaś ca bālaś ca sarvaḥ saṃmānam arhati tapovidyāviśeṣāt tu mānayanti parasparam
english: Among whom both the old and the young, every one of them, deserves honour; yet according to the distinction in austerity and learning they honour one another.

sanskrit: avidvān brāhmaṇo devaḥ pātraṃ vai pāvanaṃ mahat vidvān bhūyastaro devaḥ pūrṇasāgarasaṃnibhaḥ
english: Even an unlearned brāhmaṇa is a god, a worthy and greatly purifying vessel; but the learned brāhmaṇa is a god yet greater, like the brimming ocean.

sanskrit: avidvāṃś caiva vidvāṃś ca brāhmaṇo daivataṃ mahat praṇītaś cāpraṇītaś ca yathāgnir daivataṃ mahat
english: Whether unlearned or learned, the brāhmaṇa is a great deity, just as fire, whether consecrated or unconsecrated, is a great deity.

sanskrit: śmaśāne hy api tejasvī pāvako naiva duṣyati havir yajñeṣu ca vahan bhūya evābhiśobhate
english: For even in the cremation-ground the blazing fire is not defiled; and bearing the oblation in sacrifices it shines forth still more.

sanskrit: evaṃ yady apy aniṣṭeṣu vartate sarvakarmasu sarvathā brāhmaṇo mānyo daivataṃ viddhi tat param
english: So too, even if a brāhmaṇa engages in all manner of unworthy deeds, he is in every way to be honoured; know him to be the highest deity.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kāṃ tu brāhmaṇapūjāyāṃ vyuṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭvā janādhipa kaṃ vā karmodayaṃ matvā tān arcasi mahāmate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What reward, O lord of men, did you behold in the honouring of brāhmaṇas, and what outcome of deeds did you reckon, that you, O greatly wise one, worship them?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam pavanasya ca saṃvādam arjunasya ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue of the Wind-god and of Arjuna, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sahasrabhujabhṛc chrīmān kārtavīryo 'bhavat prabhuḥ asya lokasya sarvasya māhiṣmatyāṃ mahābalaḥ
english: There was a glorious lord, Kārtavīrya, bearer of a thousand arms, sovereign over all this world, the mighty one who ruled from Māhiṣmatī.

sanskrit: sa tu ratnākaravatīṃ sadvīpāṃ sāgarāmbarām śaśāsa sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ haihayaḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: That Haihaya of true valour ruled the entire earth, rich with the ocean's gems, with its islands, girdled by the sea.

sanskrit: svavittaṃ tena dattaṃ tu dattātreyāya kāraṇe kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya vinayaṃ śrutam eva ca
english: For a purpose he gave his own wealth to Dattātreya, setting foremost the duty of a kṣatriya, with humility and sacred learning.

sanskrit: ārādhayām āsa ca taṃ kṛtavīryātmajo munim nyamantrayata saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sa dvijaś ca varais tribhiḥ
english: And the son of Kṛtavīrya propitiated that sage, and the well-pleased twice-born one offered him three boons.

sanskrit: sa varaiś chanditas tena nṛpo vacanam abravīt sahasrabāhur bhūyāṃ vai camūmadhye gṛhe 'nyathā
english: Pressed by him to choose boons, the king spoke these words: "May I become thousand-armed in the midst of an army, yet otherwise but two-armed at home."

sanskrit: mama bāhusahasraṃ tu paśyantāṃ sainikā raṇe vikrameṇa mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jayeyaṃ vipulavrata tāṃ ca dharmeṇa saṃprāpya pālayeyam atandritaḥ
english: "Let the soldiers behold my thousand arms in battle; by my prowess may I conquer the whole earth, O man of great vows, and having won it by righteousness, may I guard it untiringly."

sanskrit: caturthaṃ tu varaṃ yāce tvām ahaṃ dvijasattama taṃ mamānugrahakṛte dātum arhasy anindita anuśāsantu māṃ santo mithyāvṛttaṃ tadāśrayam
english: "A fourth boon I ask of you, O best of the twice-born; deign to grant it for my favour, O blameless one: let the good men reproach me, should I, who lean upon them, act falsely."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa dvijaḥ prāha tathāstv iti narādhipam evaṃ samabhavaṃs tasya varās te dīptatejasaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the twice-born one said to the king, "So be it," and thus came to pass for that king of blazing splendour those boons.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa ratham āsthāya jvalanārkasamadyutiḥ abravīd vīryasaṃmohāt ko nv asti sadṛśo mayā vīryadhairyayaśaḥśaucair vikrameṇaujasāpi vā
english: Then, mounting his chariot, radiant as fire and the sun, in the bewilderment of his strength he said: "Who indeed is equal to me in valour, in steadfastness, in fame and purity, in prowess, or in might?"

sanskrit: tadvākyānte cāntarikṣe vāg uvācāśarīriṇī na tvaṃ mūḍha vijānīṣe brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyād varam sahito brāhmaṇeneha kṣatriyo rakṣati prajāḥ
english: At the end of his speech, a bodiless voice spoke from the sky: "O fool, you do not understand that the brāhmaṇa is greater than the kṣatriya; only joined with the brāhmaṇa does the kṣatriya protect the people here."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kuryāṃ bhūtāni tuṣṭo 'haṃ kruddho nāśaṃ tathā naye karmaṇā manasā vācā na matto 'sti varo dvijaḥ
english: Arjuna said: When pleased, I can bring beings into being; when angered, I likewise lead them to destruction. In deed, in thought, and in word there is no twice-born one greater than I.

sanskrit: pūrvo brahmottaro vādo dvitīyaḥ kṣatriyottaraḥ tvayoktau yau tu tau hetū viśeṣas tv atra dṛśyate
english: The first claim sets the brāhmaṇa above, the second sets the kṣatriya above; both grounds have been stated by you, yet a distinction is seen here.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśritāḥ kṣatraṃ na kṣatraṃ brāhmaṇāśritam śritān brahmopadhā viprāḥ khādanti kṣatriyān bhuvi
english: The brāhmaṇas lean upon the kṣatriya power; the kṣatriya power does not lean upon the brāhmaṇas. The brāhmaṇas, under the pretext of sacred lore, devour the kṣatriyas of the earth who give them shelter.
